title: Reviewed next-phase owning input freeze and bounded coverage consistency repairs
semantics: A consistency repair of reviewed owning metadata; it creates no historical claim, stage, transition or completed book text. Nine witness snapshots follow canonical structured chronology, including deliberate nulls. Historical dated wave counters elsewhere are preserved.

basis.note: Web tool refused 60,542,258-byte PDF. Filename 2009 and URL path 2012 are not authenticated edition dates. The whole 60,542,258-byte PDF (159 pages, SHA-256 1b1378688df94b28eb22b8095fbbe4d73c2c10422f6b9b51d972bd6600689a51) was later acquired in research scratch. Its pages 2–3 carry the decree of Archbishop Cyril Bustros of 27 January 2009, effective 15 February 2009 and valid to 31 October 2010, so the lead is an English translation of the Newton eparchy, not the undated Greek–Arabic Liturgikon.

basis.qualification: Uncertain place of origin. 1958 critical edition is a modern presentation of the witness, not a new liturgical version. ELMSS 104/105 separate two sacramentaries with different copy dates (701–750 and 751–800); ff. 100–106 (Decretum Gelasianum) are not a third sacramentary. The former single 675–725 coordinate does not fit the composite. The layers are proposed as latin-early-elmss-104 and latin-early-elmss-105, which carry the copying coordinates; this composite row has none, because the two copyings are distinct events and the date at which the parts were bound together is not established.

basis.qualification: Discovery group retained for continuity only, superseded by latin-early-scotus1482 and latin-early-aarau1483-main. USUARIUM 5840 is the 1482 printing by Octavianus Scotus (Venice) of the missal 'secundum morem Romanae ecclesiae' revised by Philip de Rotingo of Mantua, OFM Obs. (BnF B-27921, fragmentary). USUARIUM 4153 is Aarau, Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek, MsMurQ 6, a manuscript dated 1483 by its main hand at f. 86r, not a printing. The former statement that both are printings is withdrawn. Neither date alone proves a distinct recension; substantive differences and the relationship to the Roman 1474 printing remain open. The group has no coordinate because it mixes a publication date and a copying date; the individual rows carry them.
